column1: # Quarantine holds what has produced a device-level or output-level failure in
# the image lane. A row here keeps its subject out of every generation path,
# and remote/image-registry.sh reads this file rather than inferring the state
# from the tier field alone, because a quarantine has two scopes where
# remote/image-models.tsv has one row per bundle.
# scope `model` quarantines a bundle: every profile of it stays refused until
# the re-entry gate in the reason record is met, and the geometry columns read
# `-` because the exclusion is unbounded. scope `profile` quarantines one
# served shape of a bundle that otherwise generates, and width, height, steps,
# and placement name that shape exactly. The distinction is the one
# remote/quarantine.tsv draws for the language ladder: "this bundle cannot run
# here" and "this arm at this size does not retire" are different claims and
# they steer different later choices.
# failure_class is a fixed vocabulary rather than prose. The six device classes
# are the ones remote/quarantine.tsv already names --  `ring-timeout-only`,
# `gfxhub-page-fault`, `vm-protection-fault`, `device-lost`,
# `post-reset-control-failure`, `no-validated-safe-tuple` -- and the image lane
# adds two of its own. `runtime-timeout` is a run the pinned runtime's own hard
# bound ended with the device healthy. `output-validation-failure` is a run
# that produced bytes the PNG validator rejected, which is a correctness hazard
# rather than a device event.
# first_evidence and latest_evidence name the runs that opened and last
# confirmed the exclusion; reason_record points at the retained record under
# evidence/ carrying the kernel signature, the safe shapes, and the re-entry
# gate in full. Every path present must exist in the tree, so a removed record
# refuses the query rather than leaving an exclusion no reader can act on.
# The file carries a header and no rows. Nothing has been generated on the
# appliance, so no image subject has failed, and an empty ledger is the honest
# state rather than an absent authority: remote/image-registry.sh requires this
# file to be readable before it answers any query.
